manifest.title: ARX 4.0.0 Beta 1 Security Audit
manifest.description: Read-only release security audit and preserved gate evidence.

blocks.body:
## Technical summary

- **Beta 1 passed the defined dependency, SBOM, two-engine malware, CodeQL, copied-artifact tamper, secret-scan, and outbound-provider boundary checks.** These are bounded claims tied to the exact published hashes and release commit.
- **This is not a production-readiness pass.** The fuzz gate is `FAIL_INCOMPLETE`; direct standard-user lifecycle evidence is partial; the Windows binaries are unsigned; no artifact is bit-for-bit reproducible; the installer is conservatively `NOT REPRODUCIBLE`; and GitHub artifact attestations are absent.
- **No confirmed CRITICAL or HIGH finding was established.** Medium findings remain in release-verifier transport hardening, Windows signing, reproducibility, and GitHub provenance.
- **The immutable Beta 1 release was not modified.** Production PyPI remains blocked, and this report does not claim that ARX is secure.

## Defined controls passed, but production readiness remains blocked

The strongest positive evidence is artifact-specific: exact GitHub release hashes anchored malware, tamper, signature, identity, and attestation checks. The strongest negative evidence is also specific: three fuzz properties never reached ARX code, signed publisher identity is absent, rebuild bytes diverge, and GitHub provenance was never created for Beta 1. These limitations must remain visible rather than being averaged into a single score.

## Four medium findings and four lower-severity gaps need explicit review

The medium items are not interchangeable: one hardens a verification download boundary, one blocks signed Windows distribution, one blocks reproducibility claims, and one blocks GitHub provenance claims. The low items preserve incomplete, same-privilege trust-boundary, and BinSkim coverage evidence. None was automatically patched or suppressed during this read-only audit.

## The fuzz gate failed because three properties never exercised product code

The campaign completed with exit code 1: five tests passed and five failed over 67.012 seconds. Two failures are demonstrably incorrect test assumptions. Three are harness defects caused by a function-scoped temporary-path fixture, so the PE, directory metadata, and archive properties remain untested. This is `FAIL_INCOMPLETE`, not PASS, even though the failures confirm no ARX product defect.

## Defender was normal and enabled in three repeated native measurements

All requested protection fields agreed across the three observations. An earlier brief transition is preserved in the underlying evidence rather than hidden; no setting was changed during the audit.

## Both on-demand engines found no threat in the five exact reviewed targets

Microsoft Defender and isolated WSL ClamAV scanned byte-identical artifact copies. The portable executable was first reconciled to the published ZIP; the differing local executable was not treated as equivalent. No artifact was uploaded to a third party.

## Dependency and SBOM checks found no known advisory in the exact runtime closure

The immutable wheel declares only conditional `tomli>=2` below Python 3.11. Python 3.10 resolved `tomli 2.4.1`; newer Python has no runtime dependency. Pip-audit and OSV reported no advisory, and all four SBOM documents parsed successfully. This is a database-at-observation-time result, not a guarantee against unknown vulnerabilities.

## Five outputs are structurally equivalent; the installer is not reproducible

Two independent detached builds used identical pinned tool environments at the exact release commit. Wheel, sdist, portable ZIP, ARX.exe, and the checksum manifest preserve reviewed structure or normalized semantics but not bytes. Inno Setup 7.1 payload equivalence could not be independently extracted, so the installer remains conservatively `NOT REPRODUCIBLE`.

## Scope and trust anchors

**Release population.** The audit covers ARX 4.0.0 Beta 1, tag `v4.0.0-b1`, release commit `f3bce58552578df2795f292b1d4f572ee6af8e0b`, and the five public release assets identified by their published SHA-256 values.

**Result vocabulary.** `PASS_DEFINED_GATE` means only that the stated tool, scope, inputs, and rule completed as recorded. `PARTIAL`, `FAIL_INCOMPLETE`, `FAIL_ABSENT`, and `NOT REPRODUCIBLE` preserve missing evidence. A scanner severity is evidence to classify, not an automatic product conclusion.

**Exclusions.** No external target scanning, exploit development, third-party artifact upload, production signing, API-key access, paid OpenAI generation, production PyPI publication, or Phase C work occurred.

## Methodology was read-only, bounded, and release-anchored

Artifact tests began with fresh GitHub release copies and exact SHA-256 reconciliation. Source analysis used saved scanner output plus manual classification. Fuzzing targeted only ARX-owned input boundaries under bounded generation. Privilege work used manifest, ACL, source, and mocked failure evidence; destructive lifecycle testing was withheld from the non-disposable host. Network dynamics used injected mocks and ephemeral localhost servers only.

One bounded bar chart shows the reviewed finding count by severity and is explicitly not a composite risk score. Identities, categorical gate states, hashes, and exception text remain in exact tables because additional visual aggregation would obscure their distinctions.

## The host and audit-isolated toolchains were inventoried separately

Existing host tools were reused, including the intentional `arx-sec` Conda environment and the exact BinSkim path supplied for the audit. ClamAV, innoextract, and the PyPI attestation verifier were isolated from the ARX runtime; innoextract 1.9 was recorded as incompatible with Inno Setup 7.1 rather than treated as successful.

## Limitations and robustness checks

- Vulnerability databases and malware signatures are time-bound observations.
- CodeQL covered Python and Actions queries, not runtime behavior or binaries. Semgrep Actions parsing was partial.
- BinSkim did not evaluate ARX.exe without a loadable PDB; its zero rule results are no clean-scan evidence.
- The fuzz campaign is incomplete until the three harness-blocked properties run.
- Privilege conclusions lack a disposable standard-user Windows lifecycle.
- Unsigned checksums detect independent mutation but do not authenticate a coordinated replacement.
- Structural equivalence is not bit-for-bit reproducibility, and installer payload equivalence remains unproven.
- TestPyPI publish attestations verify the wheel and sdist publisher path; they do not create provenance for GitHub Windows assets.

## Recommended next steps before any production-publication review

1. Correct and independently review the fuzz harness, then rerun the three unexecuted properties.
2. Run standard-user install, launch, upgrade, denied-path, and uninstall cases in a disposable Windows VM.
3. Harden package-index download URL/redirect/size controls and the environment-derived vswhere trust boundary in a future branch.
4. Establish a trusted production signing identity and keep signing behind a protected human gate.
5. Normalize build timestamps, ordering, hash seed, and PyInstaller/Inno inputs; add an Inno 7-compatible payload comparison.
6. Add OIDC-backed GitHub artifact attestations for future exact outputs and associate the validated SBOM.
7. Keep production PyPI blocked until the user separately authorizes it after reviewing these preserved findings.

## Further questions for the next gate

- Do the corrected fuzz properties expose any product counterexample once they actually reach ARX code?
- Does a disposable standard-user Windows lifecycle confirm the static privilege model and optional post-install token behavior?
- Can the installer payload be independently compared with an Inno Setup 7-compatible method?
- Which approved production code-signing and artifact-attestation service will own future release identities?
- Which reproducibility claim—bit-for-bit or explicitly bounded structural equivalence—is required before production PyPI review?

query.description: Counts the reviewed non-informational finding register by severity and release-blocking disposition after loading the exact reviewed rows into an in-memory SQLite table.
query.sql:
WITH severity_order(severity, ordinal) AS (
    VALUES ('CRITICAL', 1), ('HIGH', 2), ('MEDIUM', 3), ('LOW', 4)
)
SELECT
    s.severity,
    COUNT(f.id) AS count,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN f.release_blocking LIKE 'Yes%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS release_blocking_count,
    COUNT(f.id) - COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN f.release_blocking LIKE 'Yes%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS review_only_count,
    'Reviewed non-informational findings' AS scope
FROM severity_order AS s
LEFT JOIN reviewed_findings AS f ON f.severity = s.severity
GROUP BY s.severity, s.ordinal
ORDER BY s.ordinal
filters: severity in CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW

metric_definitions.release_blocking_count: Rows whose release_blocking field begins with Yes.

sources.label: Host and isolated security tool inventory

security_tests.scope: Published portable ZIP and its ARX.exe
security_tests.findings: Published ZIP contains c904c0…; the earlier 1a1f03… executable is a different local build.
security_tests.recommendation: Continue anchoring binary tests to a fresh copy whose container hash matches the public release.

security_tests.scope: Native Windows host protection state
security_tests.findings: Three repeated measurements agree: Normal; service, AV, antispyware, real-time, behavior, I/O, network, and tamper protection enabled.
security_tests.recommendation: Do not alter Defender; retain timestamped raw fields when measuring release scans.

security_tests.scope: Exact wheel dependency closures for Python 3.10 and 3.11+
security_tests.findings: 0 known advisories; Python 3.10 resolves direct conditional tomli 2.4.1; 3.11+ has no runtime dependency.
security_tests.recommendation: Repeat against exact release metadata; review rather than auto-upgrade any future finding.

security_tests.scope: Python 3.10 and 3.14 dependency identities
security_tests.findings: Two CycloneDX 1.6 and two SPDX 2.3 documents parse; privacy scan found no forbidden marker.
security_tests.recommendation: Generate from final reviewed distributions and associate the validated SBOM with future provenance.

security_tests.scope: Exact wheel, sdist, portable ZIP, published ARX.exe, installer
security_tests.findings: 5/5 exact reviewed targets returned NO_THREATS_FOUND.
security_tests.recommendation: Rescan final bytes after any future build or signing operation.

security_tests.scope: Exact copied Beta 1 artifacts in isolated WSL
security_tests.findings: 5/5 exact reviewed targets returned OK; no upload and no resident daemon.
security_tests.recommendation: Keep second-engine scans isolated and require explicit approval before any third-party upload.

security_tests.scope: src, scripts, packaging
security_tests.findings: Reviewed: 0 critical, 0 high, 1 medium, 9 low, 13 informational. Medium: package-index download URL lacks an independent exact-host/redirect/size boundary.
security_tests.recommendation: Harden the future index verifier without changing immutable Beta 1; preserve all scanner evidence.

security_tests.scope: Python source/tests and GitHub Actions
security_tests.findings: Python: 1 low environment trust-boundary finding. Actions: 0 findings, but approximately 79.1% parsed with 6 pwsh-as-Bash warnings.
security_tests.recommendation: Validate the vswhere path from a trusted Windows source; retain CodeQL and workflow tests for Actions coverage.

security_tests.scope: Exact release commit; Python and GitHub Actions
security_tests.findings: 0 results across 43 Python and 17 Actions rules; 0 open or closed repository alerts at observation time.
security_tests.recommendation: Keep the pinned workflow and treat zero alerts as a defined query result, not proof of absence.

security_tests.scope: ARX-owned parsers, response parsing, redaction, and serialization
security_tests.findings: 10 tests: 5 passed, 5 failed in 67.012 s. Failures classify as 2 test-assumption errors and 3 harness defects; 0 confirmed product defects.
security_tests.recommendation: Correct and independently review the harness, then rerun all three properties that never reached product code.

security_tests.tool: mt.exe, ACL inspection, source review, pytest
security_tests.scope: Manifest, paths, installer policy, access-denial behavior
security_tests.findings: asInvoker; protected Program Files/per-user credential ACLs; permission-failure regression passed. Direct standard-user lifecycle was unavailable on the elevated host.
security_tests.recommendation: Run standard-user install/upgrade/uninstall/UAC cases in a disposable Windows VM.

security_tests.scope: Copies only: mutation, truncation, corruption, manifest, extra/missing public artifacts
security_tests.findings: 6/6 required copied-artifact cases rejected. Auxiliary non-public .txt files are outside verifier scope.
security_tests.recommendation: Retain exact upload allowlists; add independent authenticity through signing/provenance in a future release.

security_tests.scope: Published ARX.exe and installer
security_tests.findings: Both binaries are NotSigned; no trusted production code-signing certificate was found.
security_tests.recommendation: Use a protected, human-gated signing system for a future release and verify final signed bytes before checksums/provenance.

security_tests.tool: ARX build scripts / PyInstaller / Inno Setup / structural analyzer
security_tests.scope: Two detached clean builds at the exact release commit
security_tests.findings: 0 bit-for-bit; 5 structurally equivalent; installer conservatively NOT REPRODUCIBLE.
security_tests.recommendation: Normalize timestamps/order, fix hash seed/build inputs, and add an Inno 7-compatible payload comparison.

security_tests.scope: Exact TestPyPI wheel and sdist
security_tests.findings: Both subjects and SHA-256 digests cryptographically verify to the expected GitHub repository, workflow, and testpypi environment.
security_tests.recommendation: Preserve the existing Trusted Publisher identity and exact subject checks.

security_tests.scope: All five exact GitHub release artifacts
security_tests.findings: No GitHub artifact attestation was found for any reviewed Beta 1 SHA-256.
security_tests.recommendation: Attest all future release artifacts and the checksum manifest with OIDC; do not retrofit Beta 1.

security_tests.scope: Mocked provider transports and localhost only
security_tests.findings: 48 mocked and 2 localhost tests passed; redirect and oversized response rejection reached the real urllib transport. ARX exposes no inbound service, so conventional DAST is not applicable.
security_tests.recommendation: Keep external targets out of DAST; exercise outbound behavior with mocks/localhost.

security_tests.scope: Tracked/staged files and exact public release artifacts
security_tests.findings: 0 credential-shaped or host-identity findings in staged durable evidence; exact release verifier privacy scan passed.
security_tests.recommendation: Keep raw local logs with host/synthetic-secret metadata out of Git while retaining hashes and sanitized classifications.

security_tests.scope: ARX.exe from the checksum-verified published portable ZIP
security_tests.findings: The target was not evaluated because no loadable PDB was available; ignorePdbLoadError changed the process exit but still produced executionSuccessful=false and zero rule results.
security_tests.recommendation: Preserve a compatible reviewed PDB or establish documented symbol-independent BinSkim coverage for a future build; never call zero results from an unsuccessful invocation clean.

security_tests.scope: Repository tests plus audit localhost tests
security_tests.findings: 221 passed, 0 failed in 13.67 seconds.
security_tests.recommendation: Retain the same no-external-target test boundary for future audit branches.

security_tests.scope: 41 GUI tests, one isolated Windows process per test
security_tests.findings: 41 passed, 0 failed.
security_tests.recommendation: Keep GUI tests process-isolated to prevent Tk state contamination.

security_tests.scope: arx-prescanner 4.0.0b1 production PyPI state
security_tests.findings: Production PyPI has no 4.0.0b1 version; publication workflow remains disabled_manually.
security_tests.recommendation: Do not enable or dispatch production publication until every human and security gate is explicitly reviewed.

findings.finding: Published Windows executable and installer are unsigned; no production signing identity exists.
findings.security_relevance: Users cannot authenticate Windows publisher identity through Authenticode.
findings.remediation: Acquire/approve a trusted hardware-backed signing identity and use a protected human gate.

findings.finding: No tested artifact is bit-for-bit reproducible; the installer is not independently structurally verified.
findings.security_relevance: Independent rebuilds cannot reproduce the published bytes exactly.
findings.remediation: Normalize time/order/hash inputs and establish an Inno 7 payload comparison.

findings.finding: The five GitHub release artifacts have no GitHub artifact attestations.
findings.security_relevance: The GitHub assets lack an OIDC-bound build provenance record.
findings.remediation: Attest future exact outputs with a pinned action and minimal OIDC permissions.

findings.finding: The package-index verifier downloads an index-supplied file URL without a separate exact-host, redirect, or size boundary.
findings.security_relevance: A compromised/malformed index response could redirect the verifier before the existing digest check.
findings.remediation: Validate HTTPS host/port, reject redirects, and bound bytes while retaining exact SHA-256.

findings.finding: Three Hypothesis properties stopped at a function-scoped tmp_path health check before product code ran.
findings.security_relevance: PE, directory metadata, and archive robustness properties remain unexecuted.
findings.remediation: Correct the audit harness, independently review it, and rerun the bounded campaign.

findings.finding: Direct standard-user and full installer lifecycle behavior was unavailable on the elevated non-disposable host.
findings.security_relevance: The observed static boundaries do not replace real standard-user/UAC lifecycle evidence.
findings.remediation: Exercise separate standard-user/admin accounts in a disposable Windows VM.

findings.finding: ProgramFiles(x86) can influence the absolute vswhere executable path used for a fixed discovery probe.
findings.security_relevance: A hostile same-privilege environment can redirect local tool execution.
findings.remediation: Derive the installation root from a trusted native source or validate path ownership/location.

findings.finding: BinSkim could not evaluate the published PyInstaller executable because no loadable PDB was available.
findings.security_relevance: PE/MSIL rule coverage was not obtained; zero rule results came from an unsuccessful invocation and are not clean evidence.
findings.remediation: Preserve a compatible reviewed PDB or establish documented symbol-independent BinSkim coverage for a future build.

fuzz_failures.property: A bounded ZIP with generated metadata and entries is inspected without extraction, reports stable archive metadata, and does not create additional files.
fuzz_failures.counterexample: No generated product counterexample; Hypothesis stopped at setup because the property used a function-scoped tmp_path fixture.
fuzz_failures.observed: Hypothesis raised FailedHealthCheck.function_scoped_fixture before an archive was generated or scan_software was called.
fuzz_failures.expected: The harness must create fresh per-example temporary storage inside the property so bounded archives reach the scanner and extraction side effects can be measured.
fuzz_failures.security_relevance: Archive metadata and member names are attacker-controlled local inputs; bounded non-extracting inspection is a material parser-security property.

fuzz_failures.property: Bounded package.json metadata in a directory is parsed without executing content and without removing the source file.
fuzz_failures.counterexample: No generated product counterexample; Hypothesis stopped at setup because the property used a function-scoped tmp_path fixture.
fuzz_failures.observed: Hypothesis raised FailedHealthCheck.function_scoped_fixture before scan_software was called.
fuzz_failures.expected: The harness must create isolated per-example directories inside the property before generated metadata is passed to the scanner.
fuzz_failures.security_relevance: Project/package metadata is an untrusted local input boundary and must be parsed without code execution.

fuzz_failures.property: Sensitive assignments are redacted at the external boundary and the resulting bounded context remains JSON-serializable without NUL characters.
fuzz_failures.counterexample: A generated credential token also appeared independently as an ordinary background mapping key; the actual credential and labeled assignment were redacted.
fuzz_failures.observed: The product replaced the credential field and the labeled api_key assignment with redaction markers. The assertion searched the entire serialization for the generated token and found the independent background key, which the generator had not designated as a sensitive field.
fuzz_failures.expected: The property must avoid independently aliasing the chosen token into non-sensitive generated data, or explicitly define a cross-field taint-tracking requirement before asserting global token absence. The present implementation is context/pattern based, not cross-field taint tracking.
fuzz_failures.security_relevance: External-boundary redaction protects credentials and other sensitive values, but an over-broad oracle can incorrectly report leakage when unrelated data happens to equal a generated token.

fuzz_failures.property: Every bounded OpenAI response payload either yields non-empty advisory text or a ProviderError carrying a documented PARSE_FAILURE or SERVER_FAILURE status.
fuzz_failures.counterexample: Empty provider error object, empty response object, and non-object null response.
fuzz_failures.observed: The product parser raised the documented ProviderError categories SERVER_FAILURE and PARSE_FAILURE. The property then failed because it compared the uppercase enum values against lowercase string literals.
fuzz_failures.expected: The property should compare against the actual documented enum values, or compare enum members directly. The product behavior represented by these counterexamples already conforms to the intended outcome set.
fuzz_failures.security_relevance: Provider response parsing must fail closed and preserve a sanitized operational category for malformed or server-error responses.

fuzz_failures.property: A bounded, truncated PE optional header is classified as a Windows PE and produces an inspection error without an unhandled exception or mutation of the input file.
fuzz_failures.counterexample: No generated product counterexample; Hypothesis stopped at collection/execution setup because the property used a function-scoped tmp_path fixture.
fuzz_failures.observed: Hypothesis raised FailedHealthCheck.function_scoped_fixture before the product scanner was exercised.
fuzz_failures.expected: The harness must provide fresh per-example temporary storage so all generated malformed PE inputs reach the scanner under the stated bounds.
fuzz_failures.security_relevance: Malformed executable metadata is an untrusted parsing boundary; the intended robustness property remains untested by this campaign.

reproducibility.basis: PE machine, subsystem, image size, section shape, version identity, CArchive entry set, and normalized semantics of every embedded Python module match. Raw marshal ordering, the PE COFF build timestamp/checksum, .rdata, and the compressed PyInstaller overlay differ. Extracted code filenames contain no absolute path or build-user component.
All manifests name exactly the same four public binary/package artifacts and every manifest is internally valid for its build. Values differ because the artifacts are not bit-for-bit identical.

All three have the same PE shape and ARX 4.0.0 Beta 1 version resources, and both rebuilds used the same reviewed Inno script/compiler with structurally equivalent portable inputs. However .rsrc and the compressed setup overlay differ extensively. Temporary innoextract 1.9 supports only through Inno Setup 6.0.5 and could not parse the Inno Setup 7.1.0 artifact, so installed-payload structural equivalence was not independently established. The conservative classification is NOT REPRODUCIBLE.

All 989 entry names and attributes match. Exactly two raw payload entries differ: ARX.exe and _internal/base_library.zip. The executable's normalized PyInstaller code/archive semantics match; all 151 base-library bytecode modules have the same normalized semantics. The remaining 987 entry contents match exactly. ZIP timestamps and compression sizes differ.
All 88 tar member names, types, modes, sizes, link targets, and content hashes match; ownership metadata matches. Member mtimes and resulting gzip bytes differ.
All 47 entry names, uncompressed sizes, attributes, compression layout, and content hashes match. Only ZIP timestamp metadata differs across the three artifacts.
